arootah-arootah:lever:3b56acf4-471d-407a.title: Fractional Director of Technology (Advisor Network)
arootah-arootah:lever:3b56acf4-471d-407a.description: Opportunity Overview Arootah engages a curated network of senior operators to support clients across the alternative investment industry, including hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices. Advisors are deployed on project-based engagements when client needs match their expertise. Joining the network does not guarantee placement; it provides access to opportunities as they arise. Why Join the Arootah Network Alt-industry-only engagements with hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices Project-based work that fits around existing commitments Client origination and engagement management handled by Arootah; advisors focus on delivery Arootah is a talent solutions firm purpose-built for the alternative investment industry. We advise and we execute, covering the full talent spectrum from entry to exit across five services: Talent Acquisition, Fractional Leadership, Talent Development, Retention & Compensation, and Transition. Most talent firms solve one problem. Because we cover the full spectrum, we can help clients identify and solve the right one. We start with diagnosis, then deliver. Our team has run alternative investment firms at the highest levels as COOs, CFOs, and CCOs. That operator experience, combined with 15+ years of alternatives-specific recruiting and a network of 700+ vetted advisors across 18 functional disciplines, is what makes the advice credible and the execution reliable. We also draw on a network of 600+ coaches, deploying those with specific experience guiding senior executives in the alternatives industry. One industry. One talent partner. Entry to exit. Learn more: https://arootah.com/ Arootah is searching for experienced Directors of Technology to consult to our highly prestigious client base. As a consultant, you will work with our Alternative Asset Firm and Family Office clients to provide expert advice. Having previously served in this leadership role, you have specific, hands-on experience strategically supporting the efforts of the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) in building, maintaining, and overseeing the full technology (hardware and software) infrastructure and operations of a leading Alternative Asset Firm or Family Office. Best practice reviews. Developing realistic and effective action plans. Breaking apart goals into actionable steps. Advising on vendor selection and oversight. Creating and implementing policies, procedures, and control measures. Evaluating each client’s advancement toward goal actualization through key performance indicators (KPIs) and scoring matrices. Special projects or other areas of need. Assist and support the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) in managing all aspects of the day-to-day management and oversight of the full tech stack across the organization: software (full stack, mobile/web apps, AR/VR, metaverse), hardware (IT, IoT, connected devices), cybersecurity, operations (internal, external), policies, etc. Lead and manage the design, development, and deployment of new applications, systems software, and/or enhancements to existing applications. Ensure application optimization and transformation to enable corporate partners continued business growth and expansion. Supervise and implement a proactive cybersecurity, disaster recovery and business continuity planning mindset across the firm to maintain industry-leading uptime on critical technology infrastructure through successful monitoring, testing processes, and system redundancy. Provide resource management and communication across multiple product and engagement teams that rely on and are impacted by technology. Support and influence user adoption and user understanding, such as through training and demos. Optimize and supervise IT infrastructure to ensure integrity, security, and optimal performance of an office-based and remote, distributed, and growing team of employees and contractors to the standards of leading financial service organizations. Oversee and provide technical direction,

compasssurgicalpartners-compass-surgical.description: Location: Jersey Shore Ambulatory Surgery Center Address: 405 Bethel Road, Somers Point, NJ 08244 Website: https://jsasc.com/ Jersey Shore Ambulatory Surgery Center (Jersey Shore ASC) in Somers Point, New Jersey, is a modern outpatient surgery center featuring four operating rooms and a patient-centered approach to care. The center provides a cost-effective alternative to hospital-based surgery, offering services in orthopedic total joint replacement, sports medicine, podiatry, ophthalmology, spine surgery, pain management, and general surgery. Fully compliant with New Jersey Department of Health, Medicare, and AAAHC standards, Jersey Shore ASC is partnered with Compass Surgical Partners to combine clinical excellence with industry-leading operational expertise. Dedicated to safety, comfort, and personalized care, the center delivers a seamless experience from pre-op through recovery. Role Summary The Registration Specialist supports a seamless perioperative experience by coordinating patient registration, and front desk operations. This role serves as a key liaison between patients, physicians, and clinical teams, ensuring accurate scheduling, registration, communication, and administrative support while maintaining a patient-centered, professional environment. Will cross train with surgical scheduling. Tuesday-Friday, Full-time position (32 hours/week). Hours between 5:45am- 2:15pm. Expected start date late August early September What You’ll Do • Register patients accurately by verifying demographics, insurance coverage, benefits, prior authorizations, and required documentation to ensure scheduling and billing accuracy. • Review scheduling, referral, and insurance information; verify eligibility through Clariti, payer portals, and other verification resources; and determine authorization requirements for scheduled services. • Conduct authorization research and validation through payer and utilization management platforms, including eviCore, TurningPoint, Availity, PEAR, and other applicable systems. • Communicate with referring offices, patients, physicians, and staff to obtain missing information, secure required authorizations, resolve discrepancies, and coordinate patient care. • Review and validate authorization approvals, effective and expiration dates, and authorized CPT and ICD-10 codes to ensure compliance with payer requirements. • Document insurance verification, authorization status, and patient information in scheduling, registration, and electronic medical record systems. • Collect copayments, maintain patient records, and ensure confidentiality in accordance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements. • Greet patients and visitors, answer and direct telephone calls, respond to inquiries, and coordinate front desk operations to support efficient workflow and customer service. • Perform clerical and administrative duties, including record maintenance, supply management, quality improvement, safety initiatives, and upkeep of reception and patient service areas. • Maintain current knowledge of insurance verification, authorization processes, and payer-specific requirements while performing other duties as assigned. What You’ll Bring - High school diploma or GED required; healthcare patient experience preferred - Strong organizational, multitasking, and communication skills - Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced healthcare environment - Proficiency with Microsoft Windows–based systems and scheduling/registration platforms Physical Requirements - Ability to lift up to 50 pounds - Prolonged standing, walking, sitting, and frequent use of hands and arms - Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, or balance as needed WHY COMPASS SURGICAL PARTNERS? Compass Surgical Partners is a leading, independent, full-service ambulatory surgery center (ASC) development and management partner. An exclusive partner for premier health systems, Compass has built a nationwide portfolio of ASC joint ventures

cordance-cordance:greenhouse:4873120008.description: Cordance is dedicated to accelerating the growth of vertically focused business-to-business (B2B) software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies through acquisition and long-term tactical and financial guidance. We’re experienced operators and subject-matter experts with a passion for software and building businesses. We partner with founders to help them scale their businesses and realize their companies’ full potential. We look for businesses with strong leadership and high potential for profitable growth, and work together to increase year-over-year revenue, company efficiency, and impact. Cordance envisions that all companies we work with achieve their full potential. We embrace what makes each company great and build on those foundations. We believe in elevating a company as it scales, delivering dignity to the organization and its employees, and sharing a passion for building a legacy. Position Overview The Business Unit (BU) President at Cordance is the strategic and operational leader of their business unit, serving as both its product and market authority and its executive anchor. As the P&L owner, the President is accountable for setting strategy, driving disciplined growth, and ensuring scalable and efficient operations. This role requires a leader with deep industry expertise, sharp understanding of customer needs, and the ability to balance long-term vision with hands-on execution. The President will define and execute the go-to-market strategy, shape the product roadmap, establish the annual operating plan, and oversee resources and budgets to deliver sustainable business performance. They will champion customer experience, guide product strategy and engineering execution, and embed best practices in sales, pricing, packaging, customer success, and operational excellence. As the primary external face of the BU to customers, strategic partners, and the broader industry, the President will engage deeply with stakeholders while mentoring internal teams, fostering a culture of accountability and innovation, and building high-performance organizations aligned with Cordance’s long-term objectives. Define and own the BU’s vision, objectives, and long-term growth strategy, aligning with Cordance’s portfolio priorities. Develop and execute the annual operating plan and multi-year investment model, ensuring financial rigor and sustainable results. Act as the external face of the BU and Cordance to customers, partners, and industry stakeholders. Drive operational excellence across engineering, product delivery, and customer-facing teams. Team & People Leadership Build, lead, and mentor high-performing teams that embody accountability, innovation, and collaboration. databricksventures-replit-com:ashbyhq:4a.description: Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. ABOUT THE ROLE Replit is investing seriously in paid media — TV, CTV, online video, out-of-home, audio, social, and search — and we need the person who makes that investment work. This role is the internal owner of our media program: you'll direct our external media agencies, pressure-test their plans, steward the budget, and hold every dollar accountable for reaching the right audiences on the right channels at the right time. You'll report to the VP of Marketing and act as the connective tissue between our brand and growth teams and our agency partners. This is not a hands-on-keyboard activation role. You won't be living in Ads Manager — you'll be the person who briefs the agency, challenges the channel mix, catches the pacing problem before it becomes a budget problem, and translates campaign performance into decisions leadership can act on. This is the right role if you've sat on the brand side (or want to move there from a media agency), you know what a great media plan looks like and what a lazy one looks like, and you get energy from being the sharpest media mind in the room without needing to touch the platforms yourself. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Agency leadership: Serve as the primary day-to-day partner to our media agencies. Set strategy direction, write clear briefs, run planning cycles and QBRs, and hold partners accountable for performance, optimization, quality, and business results. - Plan interrogation: Review and challenge agency recommendations across every channel — TV, CTV, OLV, OOH, audio, social, search, programmatic. Catch weak rationale, frequency saturation risks, and budget misallocations before plans get approved. - Budget stewardship: Own media budget pacing, forecasting, authorizations, and reconciliation in partnership with Finance. Monitor spend and delivery mid-flight, flag risks early, and drive reallocations when the data says to. - Media strategy & planning: Lead annual, quarterly, and campaign-level planning with the agency. Make sure plans reflect our audiences, product moments, competitive pressure, and business goals — not just what's easy to buy. - Measurement & accountability: Define campaign KPIs and measurement frameworks with the agency and our analytics team. Own wrap reports, drive a test-and-learn agenda (incrementality, brand lift, MMM as we scale), and go beyond CPMs and impressions to reach efficiency and cost-per-outcome. - Executive reporting: Distill campaign and channel performance into clear recommendations for marketing leadership. Tell us what worked, what didn't, and what we should do differently — with numbers behind it. - Cross-functional alignment: Partner with Brand, Growth, Creative, Product Marketing, Social, and Comms so media plans amplify what the rest of marketing is building, and so creative assets fit the placements we're buying. REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE - 5+ years of media planning and strategy experience, either brand-side managing external agencies or at a media agency serving major consumer brands - Demonstrated experience independently reviewing and challenging agency media plans, not just executing against them - Experience managing multi-million dollar media budgets across concurrent campaigns, including pacing, forecasting, and mid-flight reallocation - Fluency across the full channel landscape: TV/CTV, online video, OOH, audio/podcasts, paid social, search, and programmatic — you can evaluate rates, rationale, and audience fit in any of them - Strong command of media measurement: reach and frequency, brand lift, incrementality testing, and marketing mix modeling - Sharp analytical skills; you can work from raw campaign data to find performance trends and budget inefficiencies, and you're at home in Excel -

This is an opportunity to raise the creative standard of an established brand while helping it evolve alongside a fast-moving business.

jobgether-jobgether:lever:8648a692-5ad6-.title: Payroll Governance, Audit & Compliance Specialist
jobgether-jobgether:lever:8648a692-5ad6-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Payroll Governance, Audit & Compliance Specialist based in Brazil. This role sits within a global payroll organization and focuses on strengthening governance, compliance, internal controls, and operational excellence. You’ll help build a standardized, well-controlled payroll environment across multiple countries and stakeholders. The position combines risk management, audit coordination, KPI monitoring, reporting, and continuous process improvement. You’ll work closely with Payroll, HR, Finance, IT, Compliance, and external providers in an international environment. The role also offers the opportunity to contribute to a broader global payroll transformation journey and shape future processes and service models. Success will require strong analytical capabilities, attention to detail, structured execution, and the confidence to challenge existing ways of working. It is an excellent opportunity for a governance-focused professional looking to make a measurable impact on global payroll operations. Drive payroll governance, compliance, and internal control initiatives across multiple countries and operational areas. Monitor payroll risks, controls, audit findings, remediation actions, and compliance requirements. Define, track, analyze, and report global payroll KPIs and operational performance metrics. Support process standardization, continuous improvement, and operational excellence initiatives across the payroll organization. Coordinate and contribute to internal and external audit activities, ensuring alignment with corporate standards and control requirements. Monitor payroll vendor performance, service levels, governance frameworks, and agreed operational commitments. Develop dashboards, reports, and data-driven insights to support management decision-making. Partner with Payroll, HR, Finance, IT, Compliance, and external providers to resolve issues and strengthen processes. Support strategic initiatives and contribute to the ongoing transformation of global payroll operations. Identify opportunities to improve controls, processes, reporting, and service delivery while challenging inefficient or outdated practices. Requirements: University degree in Business Administration, Finance, Human Resources, Accounting, or a related discipline. Professional experience in governance, internal controls, process management, audit, compliance, shared services, or a comparable function. Previous payroll experience is highly desirable. Strong knowledge of process governance, internal controls, risk management, and performance monitoring. Advanced Excel skills and experience with reporting, analytics, and Business Intelligence tools such as Power BI. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to turn data into meaningful business insights. Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic international environment. Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills across functions, regions, and external partners. Fluent English communication skills. Highly structured, detail-oriented, and organized approach to work while maintaining a broader global perspective. Ability to build effective relationships with stakeholders at different levels of an organization. Continuous-improvement mindset, proactive attitude, and willingness to challenge the status quo constructively. Experience in an industrial or manufacturing environment is a plus. Availability for an immediate start is preferred. Benefits: Permanent employment contract. Flexible work arrangement in Brazil. Market-aligned salary and benefits package. Health insurance.
